title: OOM throttling: slab-based KV allocator, soft-eviction tiers, and graceful fallback routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During peak concurrency and long-context workloads we observe transient OOMs caused by unbounded KV cache growth plus large batch compositions. Current strategies (full-model fallback or hard eviction) either cause high latency spikes or severe quality regressions.

Goal: Implement a staged, slab-based KV allocation with soft-eviction tiers, integrated with a graceful OOM throttling policy that: (1) limits tail memory growth, (2) favors latency-preserving evictions, (3) provides progressive fallbacks (reduced batch size, quantized variant, then smaller model) with deterministic retry semantics, and (4) surfaces clear observability for operators and customers.
acceptance_criteria: No user-facing 5xx OOM incidents in canary for 72h under synthetic heavy long-context workload (1–2M tokens/hr) with 95th latency within configured SLO
Memory growth rate for KV cache reduced by >=40% on workload A (long-chat simulation) compared to baseline
Automatic rollback to pre-oom safe-mode (smaller model/quantized) within 200ms of detecting sustained OOM risk
New metrics available in Console: kv_slab_utilization, kv_soft_evictions, oom_throttle_events, fallback_route_count
E2E tests that simulate intermittent OOMs and validate retry ordering and idempotency
implementation_notes: Introduce 'slab allocator' for KV cache: fixed-size slabs for common KV sizes (16B, 64B, 256B, 1KB) to avoid fragmentation and allow constant-time reclamation
Soft-eviction tiers: mark entries as 'stale' before evicting; allow per-tenant sliding window grace to rehydrate if recently used
OOM detector: sliding-window memory pressure estimator across CUDA contexts + runtime accounting per-request (estimated_token_mem + kv_reserved)
Graceful fallback pipeline: 1) dynamic batch size reduction, 2) prefer quantized variant of same model, 3) route to smaller model family, 4) enqueue to lower-priority queue with backoff
Retry semantics: deterministic idempotent retries with request fingerprinting and max 3 retry attempts; preserve ordering for chat sessions when possible
Scheduler changes: add memory-aware admission control to the batching layer; prefer mixing small short requests with long requests but cap KV reservations per batch
Compatibility: expose tunables via model config: kv_slab_limit, soft_eviction_window_ms, fallback_policy, oom_throttle_enabled
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal alpha on dev cluster with synthetic long-context load (1 node) — validate slab allocator correctness and low-level memstats (3 days)
Stage 2: Canary on 5% of production traffic using standby model group with controlled percent of long-context requests — monitor kv_slab_utilization and oom_throttle_events (7 days)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with alerting thresholds; enable auto-fallback for P1 customers only (14 days)
Stage 4: Full rollout and enable for all tenants after 30d of stable signals; document new model config params and migration notes
testing_plan: Unit tests for slab allocator allocation/free paths and soft-eviction marking
Stress tests that simulate mixed request sizes + KV growth for 48h to catch fragmentation and leak patterns
Chaos test: force OOM in a controlled canary and assert fallback pipeline and retry idempotency
Integration test: end-to-end provisioning with admission control + metrics ingestion to Console dashboards
Performance bench: ensure average latency impact <5% for typical short-gen workloads when slab allocator enabled
metrics: kv_slab_utilization: proportion of allocated slabs in use
kv_soft_evictions: count per minute of entries transitioned to soft-evict state
oom_throttle_events: count and distribution by model/region
fallback_route_count: how often requests routed to reduced-capacity variants
batch_memory_headroom: median/95th for batches at admission time
risks: Incorrect slab sizing could increase internal fragmentation and worsen memory pressure
Soft-eviction window misconfiguration may rehydrate too often and create churn
Retries and fallback routing could change semantics for conversational apps (ordering/latency) — must be opt-in per workspace
Edge case: cross-tenant KV sharing on Dedicated pools may complicate slab quotas
Monitoring noise: new metrics could generate false positives until thresholds tuned
comments: 2026-03-03 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after on-call incident where a long-history chat workload caused repeated OOM kill/restarts. Link to incident FR: https://confluence.redwood/infra/incident-2026-02-28
2026-03-04 Ravi Patel: Spike implementation plan for slab allocator drafted. Prototype available in branch 'slab-kv-allocator' — https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127
2026-03-06 Mei Chen (SRE): Ran synthetic workloads. Observed 28% reduction in peak memory but occasional regressions when many small KVs present. Adding small-slab size 16B to address this.
2026-03-08 Design review (Jonah Lee): Reviewed fallback UX in Console. Agreed to surface 'fallbacks per request' in per-route latency breakdown and add opt-out flag for strict ordering workloads.
2026-03-09 PR feedback (security): Need to ensure fingerprinting keys are hashed with workspace salt to avoid cross-tenant fingerprint leaks. Patch landed in PR 4127.
2026-03-10 QA: Integration tests failing intermittently when running chaos OOM test. Debug shows race in slab free path under concurrent evict+allocate. Assigned to @Ravi for fix.
2026-03-12 Ravi Patel: Fixed race by adding epoch-based reclamation and reduced lock granularity. Re-ran stress test for 24h with no leaks. Preparing canary rollout config.
